is_anopheles.evidence: The study tested laboratory colonies and field-caught Anopheles arabiensis mosquitoes (page 1, 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study performed species identification PCR and WHO insecticide susceptibility bioassays, but did not genotype any target-site resistance markers (kdr is only mentioned in the discussion as a potential mechanism, page 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No resistance marker genotyping was performed, so no genotype or allele counts/frequencies are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Adult mosquitoes were collected from inside houses in Karonga, northern Malawi, and reared to F1 progeny (page 2, 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research paper testing fungal infectivity and insecticide resistance.

sub_country_location.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Karonga (9° 48'51.04" S, 33° 52'.97" E), northern Malawi (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The exact collection year or dates for the field mosquitoes from Karonga, Malawi are not stated in the text.

duplicate_risk.evidence: No indication of sample reuse from other studies or consortia.

supplement.evidence: No relevant supplementary files mentioned or required; the study simply did not perform marker genotyping.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the susceptibility of laboratory strains and wild-caught Anopheles arabiensis from Malawi to infection with the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana and standard chemical insecticides. No insecticide resistance marker genotyping was conducted.
exclusion_reasons: No target resistance markers were genotyped (bioassay and fungal study only).
